questions.q: What three things does the action + artifact + tool pattern require a resume bullet to include?
options: Your job title, start date, and manager's name
What you did, what you built, and what Salesforce tool or feature you used
A list of every Salesforce cloud you have heard of
The company's total revenue and headcount
questions.explain: The lesson defines the pattern as action, artifact, and tool -- naming the work, the deliverable, and the Salesforce feature used to build it.

questions.q: Why does "Built a 5-step Record-Triggered Flow that auto-assigns Leads by territory and SLA" work better than "Worked on automating our sales process"?
options: It names a real number, a real artifact, and the specific tool used, giving a reviewer something to ask about
It is a shorter sentence
It avoids mentioning Flow Builder entirely
It uses more technical jargon, which always scores higher with ATS software
questions.explain: The lesson explains that naming a real number, artifact, and tool is what makes a bullet specific and checkable in an interview.

questions.q: In the lesson's suggested one-page structure, what comes right after the header?
options: A list of every certification currently being studied for
References from previous managers
A full history of every Salesforce release since 2017
The capstone project, broken into named deliverables with action + artifact + tool bullets
questions.explain: The structure places the capstone project early, since it carries the strongest, most specific evidence of real Salesforce skill.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about listing a certification on a resume before you have actually passed the exam?
options: It is encouraged, since employers expect it
It is required by every applicant tracking system
It should be avoided -- only list certifications you have actually earned
It only matters for architect-level roles
questions.explain: The lesson lists an unearned certification as one of the common mistakes that weakens a Salesforce resume, and that this is often the first thing a careful interviewer checks.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against numbers that don't match between a resume and a portfolio page?
options: Because a careful reviewer will notice the mismatch and it damages credibility
Because applicant tracking systems reject resumes with any numbers at all
Because resumes should never include numbers
Because portfolios are not supposed to include any of the same deliverables as a resume
questions.explain: The lesson lists inconsistent numbers across documents as a common mistake, since it is the first thing a careful reviewer will notice.
